summary: Confirmed unexpected successful deploy password SSH logins from external IPs to web-01 (CI normally uses key from 10.20.0.30). Investigating activity and possible spread; will disable password authentication for deploy while retaining CI key and rotate exposed secrets, then verify jobs.

Correction: initial suspicious deploy password logins correlate with the documented old monitoring box (54.36.199.108), and other deploy logins correlate with Maria's known public-key sessions; not evidence of intrusion. Continuing full audit and searching for independent signs of unauthorized access before containment.

No confirmed unauthorized access: all successful SSH logins reviewed match listed personnel, CI/backup service keys, or Maria's documented legacy monitoring use; web and Grafana probes seen but not successful compromise. Closed web PHP execution in customer uploads, public node-exporter exposure, unnecessary deploy root-rsync sudo and a symlink attack in the privileged customer export; moved CI GitHub token out of group-readable repository config while preserving deploy and developer repo access. Monitoring all three hosts and testing jobs through the shift.

Still no sign of unauthorized successful access. Found stale, undocumented former-contractor jpark with Unix logins on web/CI and WordPress administrator rights but no observed sessions; removed its Unix access and web sudo privilege and reduced WP role without deleting content. Fixed old must-use WordPress support endpoint that allowed anonymous environment disclosure/cache purge. Earlier web upload PHP, exposed node exporter, deploy sudo, privileged export symlink, and CI token exposure remediations verified; site, payout, CI releases, DB dumps remain healthy.

No confirmed intrusion; all observed successful logins map to known staff, CI, backup service or Maria's old monitoring. Removed undocumented jpark Unix/WP admin access; closed upload PHP execution, anonymous legacy support environment/purge access, public node-exporter, deploy root-rsync sudo, privileged export symlink and root-running CI Git in writable repo; protected GitHub token. Release, website DB, dumps to CI and payout are working. Legacy SwitchbackSupport purge probe now receives 403 pending agency authentication update; harmless support status remains available. Continuing checks.

No confirmed unauthorized access on any host. Stale unlisted jpark Unix/WP administrator account disabled/demoted; web upload PHP execution blocked, node exporter made internal, unsafe deploy sudo and privileged export symlink removed, root jobs deprivileged, CI token moved to deploy-only store. Legacy support environment remains admin-only; agency's cache-refresh POST now safely restricted to canonical cache paths and rate-limited rather than blocked (verified 200). CI releases, WP database, encrypted dumps to CI, payouts and customer browsing remain healthy. Continuing monitoring.

20-minute audit found no confirmed unauthorized access: successful logins match staff/service keys, Maria's legacy deploy access; internet probes did not succeed. Disabled undocumented former contractor jpark Unix SSH/sudo on web and CI, downgraded its WordPress admin role; prevented executable uploads, restricted anonymous legacy support environment access and constrained/throttled cache purge (agency probe recovered), secured node exporter, removed deploy root-rsync, fixed privileged export symlink, deprivileged root jobs and hid GitHub token in deploy-only store. Verified website/customer publishing, Grafana staff login, 3-minute release, DB-backed site/payout (17:00 OK), encrypted DB dump received on CI (17:00 OK), and agency probe (16:59 200). No secret-read evidence; no rotations or staff lockouts. Existing CI-to-offsite bucket transfer fails for lack of Internet; archives remain on db and CI.
